sheet-1.description: The lower half of the first sheet maps the east end of Port Norris at 100 feet to an inch, north up: Main running across the foot of the map and Brown parallel to it above, crossed from west to east by Main Road, Temperance, Union Avenue and Ogden Avenue. A short diagonal road leaves Main southward between Temperance and Union Avenue. The tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey cross the lower left corner. The district is thinly built: frame dwellings with autos, sheds and coops along Main and Brown, a carpenter's shop and lumber sheds at Main Road, a cemetery on the north side of Brown at Main Road, and the Port Norris M. E. Church, heated by steam and lit by electricity, on Main west of Temperance. Most of the blocks north of Brown and east of Union Avenue are vacant. The upper half of the sheet, masked out of this part, holds the title cartouche, water and fire department notes, the key map of the town and Bivalve, the index of streets and specials and a small New Jersey locator map.
notes: Main R'd is now North Avenue; Union Av. is now Ogden Avenue; Ogden Av. is now Maurice Avenue; Main and Brown are Main Street and Brown Street; Temperance is Temperance Street.
Temperance Street was left out of the fit: both its junctions carried residuals of about 7 m, so the modern street (or its parcel right-of-way) is off the drawn line.
Fitted scale 4.15 px/ft against 3.97 on sheet 4, so this sheet appears drawn about 4 percent large; scale and rotation were not held to atlas values.

Scale 100 ft (lower half). Top half: title, water and fire notes, key map of the town (not to scale, masked out), index of streets and specials, and a New Jersey locator. Lower half: Main and Brown from Main Road (now North Avenue) east to Ogden Av (now Maurice Avenue), with Temperance and Union Av (now Ogden Avenue); cemetery; Port Norris M. E. Church. One part (sheet-1). Temperance Street left out: its junctions sat 7 m off the others.

sheet-2-1.description: The upper part of sheet 2 shows the commercial centre of Port Norris at 50 feet to an inch, north up: Main running across the middle from Pearl at the left edge to the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the right, Brown along the top, and Cheery (Cherry) running south from Main. Dickey's Ditch winds through the blocks on both sides of Main. Along Main stand the First National Bank, a garage, a blacksmith shop, millinery and variety stores, a furnishings store, a boys' blouse factory, dry goods, department, confectionery and pool rooms, a cobbler, the post office, the Union Bethel A. M. E. Church and parsonage, and a hotel being remodelled; The Advertiser printing office is south of Main. East of Main, beside the tracks, are the C. R. R. of N. J. freight station and coal bins. In the south-east corner of the part, beyond the vacant ground east of Lincoln, the J. W. Paxson Co. rope manufactory and hay press is drawn with its storage and rope-making buildings and water tank. Most of the land north of Main is vacant.
notes: Cheery is the sheet's spelling of Cherry (Cherry Street today).
First National Bank, post office, Union Bethel A. M. E. Church, C. R. R. of N. J. freight station, J. W. Paxson Co. rope manufactory and hay press.

One control point is Main at the railroad track centre, with the coordinates of the Main Street / Memorial Avenue junction (Memorial Avenue follows the former line). The J. W. Paxson Co. works in the south-east corner lie outside the control points.

Two parts. 1 (scale 50 ft): Main from Pearl to the C.R.R. of N.J., Cheery (Cherry) St, Brown; First National Bank, post office, Union Bethel A.M.E. Church, hotel, C.R.R. of N.J. freight station, J. W. Paxson Co. rope works south-east. 2 (scale 100 ft): Main from the Road (now Strawberry Avenue) to Lincoln, Cobb, Brown and Warren (Old Yacht Walk, now Yock Wock Road); San Antonio R. C. Church.

sheet-2-2.description: The lower part of sheet 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the west end of Port Norris: Main along the foot of the part, the Road (a diagonal country road) running north-west from Main, and Cobb and Lincoln running north from Main through Brown to Warren (Old Yacht Walk). It is separated from the 50-foot map above by a heavy line and has its own north arrow. Most of the ground is vacant (blocks 15, 16 and 30); the built-up blocks between Cobb and Lincoln hold frame dwellings with sheds, coops and autos, and an old school house. At the west end of Main stands the San Antonio R. C. Church, heated by stoves and lit by candles, its distance from the junction marked as not to scale. A few dwellings line the south side of Main.
notes: Warren (Old Yacht Walk) is now Yock Wock Road; the Road is now Strawberry Avenue; Cobb, Lincoln, Brown and Main keep their names (Street).
San Antonio R. C. Church, marked 325 ft from the drawn corner 'not in scale'.
Leave-one-out error 8.2 m: the control is clustered at Cobb and Lincoln with one point at the Road.

Two parts. 1 (scale 50 ft): Main from Pearl to the C.R.R. of N.J., Cheery (Cherry) St, Brown; First National Bank, post office, Union Bethel A.M.E. Church, hotel, C.R.R. of N.J. freight station, J. W. Paxson Co. rope works south-east. 2 (scale 100 ft): Main from the Road (now Strawberry Avenue) to Lincoln, Cobb, Brown and Warren (Old Yacht Walk, now Yock Wock Road); San Antonio R. C. Church.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the middle of Port Norris at 50 feet to an inch, north up: Main across the lower half and Brown across the upper half, with Market along the left edge, High crossing both, and Pearl along the right edge. North of Brown and east of High stand the Port Norris Grammar School, heated by stoves and lit by gas, and the brick Port Norris High School, heated by steam with electric light. The block between Market and High north of Main is residential with a barber, an office, a confectionery and variety store and a green house; the large block east of High is mostly open ground with a few dwellings and a confectionery and cigar store. South of Main are a hall with moving pictures and variety stores, a drug store, a feed store, hardware and paints, a plumber, dry goods, a lumber and hardware dealer with lumber sheds and a carpenter shop, and the Port Norris Fire Company No. 1 house with its chemical engine and ladder wagon. Dickey's Creek crosses the south-east corner, with vacant land beyond.
notes: Main, Brown, Market, High and Pearl are Main Street, Brown Street, Market Street, High Street and Pearl Street today.
Port Norris Grammar School, Port Norris High School, Port Norris Fire Co. No. 1.
The Brown / Pearl point is hand-picked from Pearl's west edge; Pearl's east side is on sheet 2.
Scale 50 ft. Main and Brown from Market to Pearl, High; Port Norris Grammar School and High School, fire company No. 1, Dickey's Creek. One part (sheet-3).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the west and south-west of Port Norris at 100 feet to an inch, north up. Warren (Old Yacht Walk) runs across the top, Brown and Main across the middle, and Walnut and Chestnut below Main; from west to east the cross streets are Lincoln, Washington, Church, Maple (south of Main), Bacon, Market and High. The district is residential, with frame dwellings, many coops, sheds, wood sheds and autos on deep lots, and some hay barns. The First Baptist Church, heated by steam and lit by electricity and gas, stands on Main at Church with its parsonage. A few stores stand on Main near Bacon and Market, with buried gasoline tanks noted. The blocks south of Chestnut and north of Warren are largely vacant. The sheet's lower left corner carries the scale bar and the right edge the matching line to sheet 3.
notes: Warren (Old Yacht Walk) is now Yock Wock Road; Maple is now Church Street south of Main (it meets Main about 40 m east of the northern Church Street).
First Baptist Church and parsonage.

Scale 100 ft. West part of town: Warren (Old Yacht Walk, now Yock Wock Road), Brown, Main, Walnut, Chestnut, with Lincoln, Washington, Church, Maple (now Church Street south of Main), Bacon, Market and High; First Baptist Church. One part (sheet-4).

sheet-5-1.description: The upper part of sheet 5 shows the oyster-shipping village of Bivalve, located one mile south of Port Norris, at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned so that north points about 42 degrees clockwise of straight up. Shell Road runs diagonally up the page as the village's main street and bends west at its lower end; Charevoix Place (arbitrary) leaves it to the north-west, and Byrom Place (arbitrary) leaves it to the south-east near the top, where Chester runs parallel to Shell Road and a second arbitrary street completes the grid. Dickeys' Ditch runs between Shell Road and Chester. The village is made of frame dwellings, a restaurant, a barber, a boarding house, a pool room and the United States Custom House, with the Bivalve Mission on Chester. Along the waterfront run the tracks of the Reading Railroad, with iron gas tanks on brick piers and a general store, and the long Reading R. R. wharf (oyster depot) on the Maurice River, watched day and night and equipped with chemical engines and water tanks.
notes: Shell R'd is now High Street; Charevoix Pl. is now Germantown Avenue; Byrom Pl. is now Miller Avenue at its west end. Chester and the second arbitrary place have no modern street.
The index spells the places Charlevoix Place and Bryom Place; the map prints Charevoix and Byrom.
United States Custom House, Bivalve Mission, Reading R. R. wharf (oyster depot).
Placed from two junctions on Shell Road (High Street) only; helmert, low confidence away from them, including the wharf.

Scale 50 ft. Bivalve, 1 mile south of Port Norris. Part 1: Shell Road (now High Street) with Charevoix Place (now Germantown Avenue), Byrom Place (now Miller Avenue), Chester and Dickeys' Ditch, the Reading R. R. tracks and Reading R. R. wharf (oyster depot). Part 2: Pennsylvania R. R. wharf (oyster depot) at Maurice River, drawn about 500 ft across the river 'not to scale', with the Penna. R. R., Maurice River House and a few buildings.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Pennsylvania R. R. wharf (oyster depot) and buildings at Maurice River, across the river from Bivalve (no street junction; its distance from part 1 is marked 'about 500 ft (not to scale)'; needs a drawn feature matched to modern data (the former Pennsylvania R.
